items.title: Cal.com Went Closed Source — So I Switched to This
items.description: Cal.com went closed source in April 2026, so I went looking for a replacement. Calnode is a lean, self-hostable Calendly alternative that runs as a single Go binary with an embedded SQLite database — no Postgres, no Redis, no separate API server. In this video I break down exactly what changed with cal.com and Cal.diy, then deploy Calnode on TrueNAS using Dockge, cover event types, calendar connections, and production hardening, and show off the built-in MCP server that lets AI agents book meetings on your calendar. --- 🔗 Important Links: 📖 Wiki Page: Calnode ➤ https://wiki.serversatho.me/en/calnode Calnode GitHub ➤ https://github.com/Calnode/calnode Calnode Website ➤ https://calnode.com Calnode Deployment Guide ➤ https://github.com/Calnode/calnode/blob/main/DEPLOY.md Litestream ➤ https://litestream.io 📰 On the Cal.com license change: Cal.com: "Cal.com is going closed source. items.title: Keep Your Drives Alive Longer: TrueNAS Drive Health Guide
items.description: Hard drive prices have surged nearly 50% thanks to the AI storage crunch, so keeping your existing drives healthy matters more than ever. In this video I show you how to set up automatic SMART testing on TrueNAS after iX removed it from the GUI, how to actually read a SMART report and the 5 metrics that predict failure, plus ZFS scrubs and the other tasks that extend drive life. We cover cron jobs, the Scrutiny app, and how SMART and ZFS work together. --- 🔗 Important Links: 📖 Blog Post: Getting SMART About Your Data ➤ https://blog.serversatho.me/getting-smart-about-your-data-why-drive-health-isnt-enough/ TrueNAS Drive Health Management Docs ➤ https://www.truenas.com/docs/ Scrutiny GitHub ➤ https://github.com/AnalogJ/scrutiny Backblaze Drive Stats ➤ https://www.backblaze.com/cloud-storage/resources/hard-drive-test-data *COMMANDS USED IN THIS VIDEO* (Replace /dev/sda with your own drive. Find yours with the first command.) # List every drive and its type (sata/sas = scsi, nvme = nvme) smartctl --scan # Run a SMART test on one drive by hand smartctl -t short /dev/sda smartctl -t long /dev/sda smartctl -t short /dev/nvme0 # Test EVERY drive at once, the TrueNAS way (returns null on success) midclt call disk.smart_test SHORT '["*"]' midclt call disk.smart_test LONG '["*"]' # Portable alternative that works on any Linux box for dev in $(smartctl --scan | cut -d' ' -f1); do smartctl -t short "$dev"; done # Read the results smartctl -H /dev/sda # quick pass/fail summary smartctl -A /dev/sda # per-attribute table (the 5 metrics live here) smartctl -l selftest /dev/sda # history of tests you have run smartctl -a /dev/sda # everything at once # Abort a running test smartctl -X /dev/sda # Cross-check pool health against SMART zpool status --- 📌 Timestamps: 0:00 Intro 0:47 SMART Drama 1:36 Running SMART test from CLI 3:21 Turning SMART into a cronjob 5:08 Using Scrutiny instead 6:44 How to read a SMART test 9:27 Setting up ZFS scrub tasks 11:04 When to replace a drive 12:12 SMART + ZFS for the win 12:51 Conclusion --- 🔗 Helpful Links & Community 🛠️ Hire me for your project: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/hire 💬 Join the discussion on Discord: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/discord 📖 Check out the Wiki for setup guides & tips: ➤ https://wiki.serversatho.me/ 🎉 Support the channel on Patreon: ➤ https://links.serversatho.me/patreon Join this channel to get access to support me: ➤ https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCx0ObGO7YJZpPPf6tbHpqPQ/join 👉 Follow me everywhere ➤ https://serversatho.me ☕ Want to say thank you?
